issue.title: Suppress RepositoryCache IOException on download

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
With invalid contents in the repository cache, silence the IOException
on RepositoryCache::get and re-download an artifact when attempting to
short-circuit that operation. The repository cache can easily get into
this state when a build is interrupted while downloading into the non-
atomic repository cache destination.

Possible solution to #5390

body: In other words, Bazel doesn't notice that a download was interrupted, correct?

Correct, it doesn't notice, and it responds to invalid content on any subsequent invocations that access it via `RepositoryCache::get` (i.e. during `HttpDownloader::download`) by erroring. The only solution is to manually intervene and excise the cache entry. This is undesirable on a build fleet, as it can occur on any build abort.
I think @werkt's fix will do it. The current repository cache implementation doesn't have any eviction policy, so this is a good start to remove poisoned entries.
I believe this should be fixed with 3926e9a8d2b9ededf3a8cfac039bcaeeb7766e70. Please reopen, if the problem persists.
